## CI: AI supply-chain review of action bumps

`.github/workflows/action-bump-review.yaml` has a read-only Copilot agent
(`.github/agents/action-supply-chain-review.md`, pinned model, strict JSON verdict) assess the upstream diff of every
digest bump on `renovate/*` PRs – except bumps of the popular actions that gate on Renovate's minimum release age
instead (`.github/renovate.json`'s release-age rule: GitHub's `actions/*` and `jdx/mise-action`) – and post the verdict
as a PR comment; the job's conclusion is the check a later automerge policy gates on (shadow phase until then). The
Copilot CLI comes from mise (`[tools] copilot`, backend `aqua:github/copilot-cli`, pinned in `mise.lock`) – the mise
manager bumps it and the minor/patch automerge rule merges it like any other repo tool. Facts below verified against
Copilot CLI 1.0.112 (2026-11-16); CLI flags: [programmatic
reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-programmatic-reference), [billing in
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

- Auth env precedence is `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` > `GH_TOKEN` > `GITHUB_TOKEN` > stored login: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the
  environment that lacks the Copilot Requests permission silently shadows an existing login and fails auth. CI relies on
  this order – passing the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` bills Copilot CLI usage to the repository owner's Copilot seat on
  personally-owned repositories (no PAT needed).
- In `-p` runs every tool request that would prompt is denied. Exception: shell commands the CLI classifies as read-only
  run *without asking* – so `--deny-tool shell` (deny rules beat every allow rule and mode) is what actually closes the
  shell surface for the reviewer agent, alongside `--deny-tool write`, `--deny-tool memory`, `--disable-builtin-mcps`
  and `--disallow-temp-dir`.
- `--max-ai-credits` hard-caps a session's spend; its minimum is 30.
- `--usage-output-file` writes final usage JSON (`totalPremiumRequestCost`, `providerModelMetrics[].usage` with token
  classes) – the workflow includes it in the PR comment for cost calibration.
- Repository-level custom agents (`.github/agents/<id>.md`, id = file name without extension) are only discovered in
  prompt mode with `--trust-folder`.
- `--reasoning-effort` accepts none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Claude Sonnet 5.5 accepts `high`
  (smoke-verified).
- The compare API omits `files[].patch` for binary or oversized files (source: [compare
  commits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/compare-two-commits)): files without a trusted-side reconstruction
  are surfaced as explicit unreviewable notes and the agent's verdict rules fail closed on them.
- The reviewer input file is capped at 500000 bytes (`.github/scripts/review_input.py enrich` assembles it): the diff
  comes first and one that does not fit is truncated with an explicit marker, which the agent must treat as
  unreviewable; context sections (upstream commits with authorship and signature state, tag/release context with release
  notes, BASE-revision workflow files referencing the action, the PR description) are appended in that priority order
  only while the budget has room – an omitted section leaves a one-line note in the file.
- Files whose patch the compare API omitted get their diffs reconstructed trusted-side: the workflow fetches the old and
  new git blobs (one `git/trees/{old}?recursive=1` call maps the old-side blob SHAs; `files[].sha` is the new side's)
  and `review_input.py` inserts capped unified diffs into the diff phase – per-file cap 128 KiB with an explicit
  truncation marker, NUL-sniff binary detection, `*.map` skipped as derivative of the `src/` patches, at most 4 files.
  Verified against tj-actions/changed-files v47.0.1→v47.0.2 (the dist bundle reconstructs to ~107 KiB across 97 hunks –
  fits the budget) and nick-fields/retry v2.9.0→v3.0.0 (~1 MiB – truncates at the cap), 2026-11-17.
- Digest-to-tag matching uses `repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags?per_page=100`; its `commit.sha` is the commit the tag points
  to, so annotated tags match too (verified for both tag styles against jdx/mise-action and git/git v2.44.0, 2026-11-16;
  source: [list repository tags](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#list-repository-tags)).
- Renovate's github-actions manager rewrites a digest bump together with the pin's trailing `# vX.Y.Z` version comment
  and touches nothing else in the file (verified on PR #29's diff, Renovate 44, 2026-11-16). The review workflow's
  tamper guard normalizes a pin whose ref is exactly a digest followed only by whitespace or the version comment on that
  basis: digest+comment rewrites of any pin pass, any other edit to the workflow – including a longer or floating ref –
  trips.

## CI: Branch protection and platform-native automerge

`main` is branch-protected with required status checks (no review requirement, admin bypass on). Dependency-bump PRs
merge via GitHub's **native auto-merge**: `.github/renovate.json` sets `platformAutomerge: true`, the repository setting
"Allow auto-merge" is on. Renovate enables auto-merge on the PR and GitHub merges it the moment every required check is
green on the PR head – merging does not wait for the hosted Renovate app's run cadence. The required checks are the
*only* merge gate in this configuration – with none set, GitHub merges auto-merge PRs without waiting for CI (GitHub
docs' own warning) – so the required set below must stay in sync with the workflows: renaming a job, adding an app (its
`Lint app <name>` leg), or dropping a check needs the same change in the protection rule.

Required set (contexts are the job `name:` strings):

- `Find apps`, `Mise check (lint + validate)`, `Device-visible app changes require a version bump`, `Initialize builds`,
  `Build gate` – unconditional on every PR. `Build gate` (builder.yaml) folds the conditional `Build <app>` matrix into
  one static context: required checks must report on every PR, the matrix only runs when init finds changed app files,
  and the multi-arch build is a real gate for apk-pin PRs – the per-arch Alpine index race can fail one arch while the
  other passes (§"apk package version policy"). It passes on `skipped`, fails on any other non-success matrix result.
- `Lint app hd-idle`, `Lint app hickory-dns`, `Lint app nfs-server` – the find-addons matrix is repo-static (three
  apps).
- Deliberately not required: `Action supply-chain review (shadow)` (path-filtered, shadow phase – see §"CI: AI
  supply-chain review of action bumps"), `Build <app>` (dynamic matrix names; skipped legs never report), the
  apk-bump/publish-reconcile/skills-update workflows (post-merge or scheduled only).

Protection specifics: `strict: false` – no "require branches up to date". With it on, every merge invalidates every
other in-flight PR, and each invalidation becomes a rebase plus a fresh CI cycle; without it, a PR's CI certifies its
head against the `main` of that moment and the merge lands on a newer tip. Accepted trade for dependency bumps:
file-disjoint updates re-validated against a slightly newer tip add no signal (per-dep rationale in renovate.json's rule
descriptions). `required_linear_history: true` keeps the `automergeStrategy: rebase` property (one conventional commit

Schedules: `after 8pm on sunday` + `before 8am on monday` (12 h strip, Europe/Zurich, all managers incl. apk). The
hosted app's runs are irregular and `updateNotScheduled` (default `true`) suppresses branch/PR creation outside the
window, so a missed run pushes a whole week's bumps out by a week. Batch intent: PRs open Sunday evening, required

required context can never report it – they must be merged or rebased before the rule applies.

`.github/workflows/action-bump-review.yaml` has a read-only Copilot agent
(`.github/agents/action-supply-chain-review.md`, pinned model, strict JSON verdict) assess the upstream diff of every

instead (`.github/renovate.json`'s release-age rule: GitHub's `actions/*` and `jdx/mise-action`) – and post the verdict
as a PR comment; the job's conclusion is the check a later automerge policy gates on (shadow phase until then). The
Copilot CLI comes from mise (`[tools] copilot`, backend `aqua:github/copilot-cli`, pinned in `mise.lock`) – the mise
manager bumps it and the minor/patch automerge rule merges it like any other repo tool. Facts below verified against
Copilot CLI 1.0.112 (2026-11-16); CLI flags: [programmatic
reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-programmatic-reference), [billing in
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

- Auth env precedence is `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` > `GH_TOKEN` > `GITHUB_TOKEN` > stored login: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the
  environment that lacks the Copilot Requests permission silently shadows an existing login and fails auth. CI relies on
  this order – passing the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` bills Copilot CLI usage to the repository owner's Copilot seat on
  personally-owned repositories (no PAT needed).
- In `-p` runs every tool request that would prompt is denied. Exception: shell commands the CLI classifies as read-only
  run *without asking* – so `--deny-tool shell` (deny rules beat every allow rule and mode) is what actually closes the
  shell surface for the reviewer agent, alongside `--deny-tool write`, `--deny-tool memory`, `--disable-builtin-mcps`
  and `--disallow-temp-dir`.
- `--max-ai-credits` hard-caps a session's spend; its minimum is 30.
- `--usage-output-file` writes final usage JSON (`totalPremiumRequestCost`, `providerModelMetrics[].usage` with token
  classes) – the workflow includes it in the PR comment for cost calibration.
- Repository-level custom agents (`.github/agents/<id>.md`, id = file name without extension) are only discovered in
  prompt mode with `--trust-folder`.
- `--reasoning-effort` accepts none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Claude Sonnet 5.5 accepts `high`
  (smoke-verified).
- The compare API omits `files[].patch` for binary or oversized files (source: [compare
  commits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/compare-two-commits)): files without a trusted-side reconstruction
  are surfaced as explicit unreviewable notes and the agent's verdict rules fail closed on them.
- The reviewer input file is capped at 500000 bytes (`.github/scripts/review_input.py enrich` assembles it): the diff
  comes first and one that does not fit is truncated with an explicit marker, which the agent must treat as
  unreviewable; context sections (upstream commits with authorship and signature state, tag/release context with release
  notes, BASE-revision workflow files referencing the action, the PR description) are appended in that priority order
  only while the budget has room – an omitted section leaves a one-line note in the file.
- Files whose patch the compare API omitted get their diffs reconstructed trusted-side: the workflow fetches the old and
  new git blobs (one `git/trees/{old}?recursive=1` call maps the old-side blob SHAs; `files[].sha` is the new side's)
  and `review_input.py` inserts capped unified diffs into the diff phase – per-file cap 128 KiB with an explicit
  truncation marker, NUL-sniff binary detection, `*.map` skipped as derivative of the `src/` patches, at most 4 files.
  Verified against tj-actions/changed-files v47.0.1→v47.0.2 (the dist bundle reconstructs to ~107 KiB across 97 hunks –
  fits the budget) and nick-fields/retry v2.9.0→v3.0.0 (~1 MiB – truncates at the cap), 2026-11-17.
- Digest-to-tag matching uses `repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags?per_page=100`; its `commit.sha` is the commit the tag points
  to, so annotated tags match too (verified for both tag styles against jdx/mise-action and git/git v2.44.0, 2026-11-16;

  tamper guard normalizes a pin whose ref is exactly a digest followed only by whitespace or the version comment on that
  basis: digest+comment rewrites of any pin pass, any other edit to the workflow – including a longer or floating ref –
  trips.

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-workflow (skill)

Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild) – squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged
  changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-markdown (skill)

Markdown formatting conventions for this repository – panache owns all formatting, rumdl is the semantic second linter, and specific constructs break the toolchain. Use when writing or editing any Markdown file here.

## Content

# Markdown conventions

## Formatting ownership

- panache (`panache.toml`) owns ALL formatting: `mise run fmt` reflows prose to the 120-char width. Never hand-wrap
  prose – write naturally and let `fmt` shape it.
- The lint gate runs `panache format --check` and `panache lint` over tracked `.md` files – the lint adds semantic
  checks (references, heading hierarchy, …).

## rumdl

- Second linter (`.rumdl.toml`, markdownlint-rules-rich); its own reflow is disabled (its fill state disagrees with
  panache's), so MD013 is a pure width check: code blocks exempt, lines whose only overrun is an unbreakable code span
  forgiven. panache's reflow breaks around struck spans, never inside them (it leaves a too-long span overwide on its
  own line), and MD013 does not exempt struck spans the way it exempts code spans: keep struck spans within the
  120-column width.
- Inline HTML is allow-listed per element, not per file (MD033), see `.rumdl.toml` for the currently allowed HTML tags;
  every other tag fails the lint, READMEs included. Reach for Markdown constructs (links, images, emphasis, code spans)
